name: Bandar Laddu
subtitle: the coarse gram-flour laddu of Machilipatnam, more crumb than sphere

ingredients.note: coarse besan is the point; fine flour gives a dense, pasty laddu

prepNotes: The boondi is made loose and coarse rather than as neat pearls, which is what gives Bandar laddu its crumbly bite.
It is a GI-tagged sweet from Machilipatnam, which the British called Bandar.

steps.text: Whisk the besan with the water into a thick batter that falls in ribbons.
Heat half the ghee. Pour the batter through a slotted spoon so it falls in irregular drops and fry until pale gold.
steps.tip: Pale gold, not brown. It cooks again in the syrup.

steps.text: Drain and crush the fried boondi coarsely between your palms.
Fry the cashew and raisins in a spoonful of ghee and stir them through with the sugar and cardamom.
Pour over the remaining warm ghee and mix. While still warm, press firmly into balls.
steps.tip: Warm is essential. Cold mixture will not hold and you will be left with sweet crumbs.

storage: Keeps 10 days in an airtight tin at room temperature. The ghee firms up but the laddu stays crumbly, which is how it should be.
